open_points.subject: OwnerSession idle-time origin
open_points.text: “changed by the owner's requests: the instant of its last request” and A13's validity rule uses “s.last_action + 30min”, but no initial last-request instant is stated
open_points.question: At sign-in, what value initializes the session's last-request instant before the owner makes another request?
options: Initialize it to the sign-in instant
Leave it absent and apply no idle timeout until the first later request
Treat the sign-in itself as an owner request by a separate rule
open_points.default_guess: Initialize it to the sign-in instant.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession expiry fact
open_points.text: “its expiry at the latest”
open_points.question: What exact instant does the stored expiry denote: the fixed eight-hour deadline, the current idle deadline, or the earlier of both?
options: The fixed eight-hour deadline
The current thirty-minute idle deadline
The current earlier of the absolute and idle deadlines
open_points.default_guess: Store the fixed eight-hour deadline and derive the idle deadline from the last-request instant.

open_points.subject: Pending confirmation replacement
open_points.text: “its pending confirmation values ... each kept until used, replaced or the session ends”
open_points.question: When is a pending confirmation value replaced, and may one owner session hold several live values for different actions or targets at once?
options: Only one value exists; showing any new confirmation replaces it
One value per action and target exists; a matching new step replaces it
Any number of values may coexist until use or expiry
open_points.default_guess: Keep one value per action and target, replacing the previous matching value.

open_points.subject: Uploaded import file consumption
open_points.text: “the import file uploaded in it, each kept until used, replaced or the session ends”
open_points.question: Does a refused confirmation submission count as using the uploaded import file, or does it consume only the confirmation value while retaining the file for a newly shown confirmation step?
options: Any confirmation submission drops the file
Only an accepted import drops the file
A refused submission keeps the file unless the refusal says the file itself is invalid
open_points.default_guess: Keep the file after a refused submission and require a new confirmation value.

open_points.subject: Create replay check precedence
open_points.text: A01 says a repeat passes stages “(1) to (4)” and “No other check of stage (6) is made again”, while A04 says “Only an action that passes all six may be a repeat that changes nothing”
open_points.question: Does a create replay bypass stage 6 after stages 1–4, or must it pass every applicable stage including lifecycle and customer-eligibility checks?
options: A01 is the special rule and bypasses stage 6
A04 controls and every repeat passes stage 6
Only the particular stage-6 checks expressly waived by A01 are skipped
open_points.default_guess: Treat A01 as a narrow exception and skip only the original create eligibility checks it identifies.

open_points.subject: Concurrent creates with one request id
open_points.text: “A create whose request id an existing record ... carries is a repeat” and request ids must be unique, but no rule says how simultaneous first uses of one request id are serialized
open_points.question: What are the exact results when two concurrent creates of the same model first present the same request id, with equal or different facts?
options: Serialize them; equal facts produce one creation and one replay, differing facts produce one creation and one refusal
Refuse both concurrent calls
Allow either call to win but retry the loser only after a uniqueness failure
open_points.default_guess: Serialize by request id; one creates, and the other is evaluated as a replay.

open_points.subject: Agent set check stage
open_points.text: A04 places “for agent authority, the session and its set” in stage (2), but also places “not in the set” among stage (6) lifecycle checks
open_points.question: At which stage is a project outside the agent session's granted set checked?
options: Stage 2 only
Stage 6 only
Stage 2 for hiding existence, with no second set check at stage 6
open_points.default_guess: Check it at stage 2 only so it hides every later failure as A10 requires.

open_points.subject: CSRF on owner reads
open_points.text: A04 says every operation checks, for the owner, “a valid owner session, then its CSRF value”, while A13 requires CSRF for “Every change in the owner interface”
open_points.question: Must read-only owner-interface requests carry and pass the CSRF value, or only state-changing requests?
options: Only state-changing requests require CSRF
Every owner-interface request requires CSRF
Reads require CSRF only when submitted by a form method
open_points.default_guess: Require CSRF only for state-changing requests.

open_points.subject: Accepting a request for an already granted project
open_points.text: A05 makes “granting a project already in a session's set” a no-op, while answering an access request always clears the pending request and may grant the project
open_points.question: If the owner accepts a pending request by choosing a project already in the set, is the action a no-op, or does clearing the request move the access version and write a grant audit entry?
options: Clear the request, move the version, and write the grant entry
Clear the request and move the version without a grant entry
Treat the whole answer as a no-op
Refuse the answer because the project is already granted
open_points.default_guess: Clear the request and move the version, but write no grant entry because the granted set did not change.

open_points.subject: Ordering of conflict collections
open_points.text: A06 orders the import mapping's projects, rooms, pointers and Customers, while A16 also returns “every id that conflicts with one production holds” without declaring an order for those conflicts
open_points.question: In what deterministic order are import conflict entries returned?
options: By identity kind, then id
In file order
Grouped under each mapped record using that record's list order
open_points.default_guess: Order by identity kind and then by id using Unicode code-point order.

open_points.subject: Owner session cookie policy
open_points.text: The cookie is “scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and same-site policy enforce these statements, and may the cookie be sent over plain HTTP when Registry is reached locally?
options: Always Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict with host-only scope
Secure only for remote HTTPS, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict
Secure and HttpOnly with SameSite=Lax
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only cookie that is always Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.

open_points.subject: Simultaneous audit append and dated erasure
open_points.text: Entries are appended by accepted changes and removed by a dated erasure “in the same transaction”, but no ordering rule covers an append racing that erasure
open_points.question: If another action appends an entry whose instant is before the cutoff while the dated erasure runs, must that entry be removed or may it survive depending on commit order?
options: Serialize all audit appends and erasures by commit order
The erasure removes every qualifying entry even if concurrently appended
A concurrent append always survives once its own transaction commits
open_points.default_guess: Serialize audit mutations; an append committed before the erasure is eligible for removal, while one committed after survives.

open_points.subject: Import mapping interaction
open_points.text: “The owner uploads the export file. Registry ... answers the mapping” but the same mapping contains “for each project the owner picks” and owner-supplied names, aliases and Customer values
open_points.question: When and how are picks and replacement values supplied relative to upload, mapping display and confirmation, and does changing any of them require Registry to generate a new mapping?
options: Upload first, then submit picks and values to generate the confirmable mapping
Upload, picks and values arrive in one request
Registry first shows all projects, then dynamically accepts picks without regenerating the mapping
open_points.default_guess: Upload first, then submit picks and values to generate a new mapping and confirmation step.

open_points.subject: Confirmation after file replacement
open_points.text: Rule 2 says another upload replaces and drops the earlier file, while required test 3 says “Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded applies only the file whose digest the confirmation named”
open_points.question: Must confirmation of the old mapping be refused because its file was dropped, or must Registry retain and apply the old file rather than the newly uploaded one?
options: Refuse because the old file is no longer kept
Retain both files and apply the digest-bound old file
Apply the newly uploaded file only if its digest matches
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the old confirmation because its file is no longer kept.

open_points.subject: Empty import selection
open_points.text: The owner may pick “any subset” and an accepted import permanently creates the migration closure, but no rule addresses an empty subset
open_points.question: May the owner confirm an import with no project selected, thereby closing the one-time migration without importing anything?
options: Refuse an empty selection
Accept it and permanently close migration
Accept it as a no-op without creating the closure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse an empty selection.

open_points.subject: Imported Customer identity mapping
open_points.text: The mapping shows each Customer the import will make and its v1 value, but does not say when the new Registry-minted customer_ref is allocated or whether the owner sees it before confirmation
open_points.question: Is each new customer_ref minted and displayed in the mapping, reserved until confirmation, or minted only inside the import transaction?
options: Mint and reserve it when showing the mapping
Show a deterministic proposed id but persist it only on confirmation
Mint it only inside the accepted import transaction
open_points.default_guess: Mint it inside the import transaction and show only the source-to-new-Customer mapping before confirmation.

open_points.subject: Import file digest
open_points.text: The confirmation and migration closure identify the file “as a digest”, with no digest algorithm, canonical input or collision requirement
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and exact bytes define the file identity used for confirmation and the closure?
options: A cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A digest of a canonical parsed representation
A release-selected digest declared in State 6
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: Configuration item namespace
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other” and “an unknown item fails the start”
open_points.question: What collection is inspected for unknown items: every process environment variable, a Registry-specific namespace, or a dedicated configuration document?
options: Only keys in a dedicated Registry configuration document
Only environment variables with a Registry prefix
Every environment variable visible to the process
open_points.default_guess: Validate only a dedicated Registry configuration namespace.

open_points.subject: Secret byte length
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long”
open_points.question: Which representation is measured when configuration supplies text: encoded bytes, decoded binary bytes, or characters, and which encoding or decoding is required?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the configured text
Bytes after mandatory base64 decoding
Unicode character count
open_points.default_guess: Require base64-encoded secrets and measure the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: Missed daily backup run
open_points.text: Registry backs up “once a day at 03:00 UTC” and failures are retried “at the next run”, but startup or downtime across 03:00 is not covered
open_points.question: What happens when Registry is stopped at 03:00 UTC or remains stopped for several scheduled days?
options: Run one catch-up backup at the next start
Wait until the next 03:00 UTC
Run one backup for every missed day
open_points.default_guess: Run one catch-up backup at startup if no successful backup exists for the current UTC day.

open_points.subject: Thirty-day backup retention
open_points.text: Registry deletes backups “more than 30 × 24 hours before”, while the consequence says an erasure reaches backups “at most 30 days after it”
open_points.question: Are backups deleted at age greater than or equal to 30 days, or only after they become strictly older, which can retain them until the following daily run?
options: Delete at age greater than or equal to 30 days
Delete only when strictly older than 30 days
Delete by UTC calendar date rather than elapsed hours
open_points.default_guess: Delete at age greater than or equal to 30×24 hours.

open_points.subject: Backup failure invariants
open_points.text: The formal invariant says “after a run: no backup older than 30 days exists” and “every kept backup is ... checked”, while rule 6 allows a deletion to fail and rule 4 requires deletion of a failed check, which may itself fail
open_points.question: What state is permitted after deletion of an expired or failed-verification backup fails?
options: Old or invalid files may remain and the formal invariants are conditional on successful deletion
A failed deletion makes the whole run retry until the invariants hold
Registry quarantines the file so it is no longer considered a backup
open_points.default_guess: Quarantine failed or expired files and make the invariants apply only to recognized usable backups.

open_points.subject: Backup audit sequence metadata
open_points.text: A backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and verification checks that “its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”, although all audit entries may have been erased while the durable last-ever sequence remains
open_points.question: What value is recorded and checked when the backup contains no audit entry, or when its highest surviving entry is lower than the durable last-ever sequence counter?
options: Record the highest surviving entry or null
Record the durable last-ever sequence counter separately from the highest surviving entry
Record both values
open_points.default_guess: Record both the durable last-ever counter and the highest surviving audit-entry sequence.

open_points.subject: Decrypted backup temporary file
open_points.text: Registry decrypts a backup “into a temporary file in the backup location” and then “removes the temporary file”, but interruption between those steps is not covered
open_points.question: How are plaintext temporary files protected and removed after a crash or restart?
options: Never write plaintext to disk; verify through a streaming or encrypted temporary representation
Create a restricted temporary file and delete stale verification files at startup
Rely solely on full-disk encryption and manual cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Avoid persistent plaintext by decrypting into an anonymous or immediately unlinked restricted temporary file.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption format
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” without naming authenticated encryption, nonce handling, file format or tamper detection
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption scheme and metadata format must implementations use?
options: A fixed AEAD scheme and versioned envelope declared here
An implementation-selected AEAD scheme recorded in each backup
Encryption without authentication plus the store integrity check
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned envelope with a fixed modern AEAD scheme and a fresh random nonce.

open_points.subject: Restore across releases
open_points.text: A backup is checked against “the store version of its release”, while startup accepts only “the store version of the running release” and restore simply replaces production's store
open_points.question: How is a backup from an earlier release restored after production has moved to a release with another store version?
options: Run the old release, restore, then execute the normal release migration
Permit the current release to migrate the restored store before serving
Declare older-version backups unrestorable after a release change
open_points.default_guess: Restore with the backup's release and then apply the normal release migration while stopped.

open_points.subject: Post-restore security-state replay
open_points.text: After restore the owner repeats “every erasure, restriction and end of a relationship made after the backup”, but lifts, resumptions and later changes to the same subjects are not mentioned
open_points.question: Does the owner replay every intervening action in order, or restore only the final effective state, especially when a restriction was later lifted or an ended relationship later resumed?
options: Replay every relevant action, including lifts and resumptions, in original order
Apply only the final effective restricted and ended states
Repeat only restrictions and endings even if later reversed
open_points.default_guess: Apply the final effective security and retention state, including lifts and resumptions, from the external review record.

open_points.subject: Release verification
open_points.text: “A dependency changes only by a new release, verified as any release”
open_points.question: What constitutes verification of a release, who or what performs it, and what evidence must exist before that release may run?
options: A defined automated verification pipeline and signed release manifest
Owner approval after required tests pass
Digest matching alone is the verification
open_points.default_guess: Require the release manifest and dependency digests to pass the defined automated test and build verification before owner approval.

open_points.subject: Security-review reopening
open_points.text: “A change to a decision a category names reopens this review”
open_points.question: Do changes to affected State 0 text, State 1 models, or new State 2 decisions also reopen the review when they alter a category but are not one of its currently named decisions?
options: Any security-relevant change to States 0–2 reopens affected categories
Only changes to the expressly referenced decisions reopen them
A later reviewer decides manually whether an unreferenced change matters
open_points.default_guess: Reopen every affected category for any security-relevant change to States 0–2, including model changes and new decisions.
